# the contributor independent audit: simplex-container Minkowski defect transfer

Read `candidate e2c21ddfc5abb8ca` in full.
Result: PASS, no correction required. Its verifier was rerun:3065
exact checks PASS. This is not an OC completion claim.

The common facet-normal container of each full summand is explicitly
a positive translated homothet of the standard simplex. The offsets
of their weighted Minkowski sum are the corresponding support values
of the actual sum. If the enclosing simplex's facets touch that sum,
the two simplices coincide. The coordinate argument explicitly avoids
the false claim that translating every summand by the same vector
commutes with a weighted sum of weights not summing to one.

The volume deficit expansion uses the standard finite Minkowski
polynomial, and monotonicity in each mixed-volume argument makes every
coefficient difference nonnegative. The pure terms have exactly the
weights lambda_i^d. Retaining them gives constant1; zero weights and
individual translations cause no difficulty. When the reference body
only contains the sum, its extra ordinary volume remains in the bound.

The global ordinary stability estimate converts correctly to an absolute
error using a proved enclosing-volume ratio. Maximal inscribed simplex
normalization gives lambda_j>=-1, and the outer simplex has homothety
ratio d+2, hence volume ratio at most(d+2)^d. No simplex approximation
of a mixed-integer union or lattice-preserving affine assertion is made.

The exact equality example is valid for full summands with fixed positive
weights. A corner truncation A_e of T has Hausdorff-infinity distance
e/d from T. The new contact/locality theorem bounds every minimizing
simplex's corresponding facet centroid inside a neighborhood where
the only boundary of A_e is the original facet. All other barycentrics
are strictly positive and the truncating plane is absent there. The
facet's supporting plane is consequently forced, proving unique
minimum container T with the stated explicit smallness range.

The exact identity A_e+tT={x>=0:e<=sum x<=1+t} is proved by a
scalar decomposition and yields minimum container(1+t)T. Its missing
volume equals the first summand's missing volume and the other summand
has zero defect. Thus constant1 is attained, not merely approached.
The polynomial formula also proves that every cross mixed-volume
defect can vanish although one summand is nonsimplex. Such cross terms
therefore cannot alone justify a strict homothety conclusion.
